title: Token-bucket shard collision causing billing divergence during lease handoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers observed short-lived spikes in allowed requests and corresponding overcharges during scheduled shard lease reassignments. This ticket captures the investigation into an observed token-bucket shard collision during lease handoff that led to duplicate credit application and billing divergence across per-key and per-route quotas.

Why this matters: The rate engine must provide monotonic, single-source accounting for credits/debits. A race that allows two shards to both apply burst credits or accept the same debit path undermines correctness and can result in customer overbilling, incorrect throttling behavior, and SLO violations.

Observed symptoms:
- Short bursts (30s–3min) where request rates exceed configured per-route burst limits without throttling.
- Corresponding spike in metering events and invoices for affected orgs.
- Incidents coincide with lease handoff windows and cross-zone shard migration events.
- Affected routes have alias mappings and recent route renames.

Repro steps (stable repro is nontrivial; here is a best-effort sequence):
1) Configure small token-buckets (burst=50 tokens, refill-rate low) per-route for org X.
2) Start steady stream of requests slightly under threshold from two different edge nodes that map to different shard replicas.
3) Trigger a lease transfer for the shard (kill primary, initiate handoff) during a refill tick boundary.
4) Observe both old and new shard accept debits/credits for the same timewindow; rate engine logs show two successful debit confirmations with different shard-ids.

Key log snippets: (redacted)
- [2026-02-14T15:23:01Z] shard-leader(sha-21): applying refill +30 tokens for key=orgX/routeY epoch=42
- [2026-02-14T15:23:01Z] shard-follower(sha-07): accepted refill +30 tokens for key=orgX/routeY epoch=41
- [2026-02-14T15:23:01Z] debit-applier(sha-07): debit -12 tokens request_id=abc123 status=OK
- [2026-02-14T15:23:01Z] debit-applier(sha-21): debit -12 tokens request_id=abc123 status=OK

Initial hypothesis: Lease handoff and epoch reconciliation logic allow a short window where both the old and new shard think they are authorized to perform token updates. Coupled with per-key alias remapping and route rename state that is not atomically visible during migration, two independent refill/debit sequences can both succeed. Contributing factors: non-idempotent debit application, insufficient epoch gating on refill path, and the refill tick being coarser than lease transition events.

Investigation work done so far:
- Collected correlated logs from shard leader election, refill scheduler, and debit appliers for three affected customers. (Links in attachments)
- Replayed a controlled migration in staging with enhanced debug flags to capture epoch and lease tokens. Confirmed both shards applied refills within a 50–200ms window.
- Instrumented meter aggregator to add shard_id and lease_epoch to outgoing metering events (short-term tracing only).
- Wrote a small repro harness that simulates lease handoff and concurrent refill+debit; added to local testbed.

Immediate mitigations (hotfix plan):
- Implement soft-block: on lease handoff, reject refill requests from the old shard if a newer epoch has been observed for the key (requires cross-shard epoch propagation). Rapid PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/3214.
- Add an at-most-once debit guard: require debit idempotency token (request_id) to be checked against a transient in-memory cache for a 2s window. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/3220.
- Short-term operational: increase shard handoff throttle windows (reduce frequency of scheduled rebalances) and schedule heavier migrations outside peak hours.

Proposed long-term fix:
1) Strengthen lease epoch semantics: make refill+debit paths check a canonical lease_epoch persisted in the shard metadata store before applying state changes. If mismatch, abort and redirect to current leader.
2) Make debit application idempotent at the write-path level by using a monotonic per-request token stored in the shard-level persistent log (compact retention).
3) Add an end-to-end integration test in our k8s staging that simulates shard failover under live refill ticks and asserts no duplicate debit/refill events.
4) Enhance meter event schema to include shard_epoch and canonical_shard_id for future reconciliations.

Backfill and customer remediation:
- Produced a reconciliation script that computes duplicate debits by grouping on request_id and timestamp windows; suggested credits for impacted customers have been computed for orgs A, B, C and uploaded to billing-asst (internal doc).
- Requested Finance to hold billing adjustments pending automated verification (see confluence link).

Next steps (actionable):
- [P0] Merge and canary PR/3214 (soft-block) to staging and monitor for symptom reduction (assigned Marco). Target date: 2026-03-12.
- [P0] Merge idempotency PR/3220 and enable for high-risk shards only (progressive rollout).
- [P1] Implement persistent epoch gating and add e2e tests (design spike scheduled).
- [P2] Run reconciliation backfill and confirm charge reversals for affected customers; communicate via CS and GA.

Artifacts and links: 
- Staging reproducer + harness: internal://kb/rate-repro/ENG-790321
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/3214, https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-engine/pull/3220
- Dashboards: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/rate-engine/duplicate-debits
- Confluence writeup & remediation plan: https://rwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RE/pages/790321

Owner notes: We must avoid superficial fixes that tolerate duplicate application; correctness requires a combination of epoch gating and idempotent application semantics. The short-term soft-block reduces blast radius and buys time to implement the persistent-solution.
